subject.title: feat(tui): inline image rendering via pi-tui Image component

question: Should TUI inline image rendering read absolute MEDIA paths emitted by tool results from the host TUI process, or should it render only trusted media-store/base64 payloads with a text fallback?
rationale: The implementation choice affects whether model/tool output can cause host-local file reads, and that boundary is a maintainer product/security decision rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Restrict to trusted payloads
options.body: Render only base64 or media-store references that OpenClaw already classifies as displayable, and leave arbitrary local paths visible as text.

options.title: Allow guarded local paths
options.body: Accept the current local path model after maintainers document the trust boundary and require live proof across supported and unsupported terminals.

options.title: Pause this feature
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open and close or defer this PR until terminal-image scope and safety expectations are settled.

recommendation.title: Restrict to trusted payloads
recommendation.body: Render only base64 or media-store references that OpenClaw already classifies as displayable, and leave arbitrary local paths visible as text.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the TUI component surface and the adjacent image_generate workflow, making him the strongest routing candidate for the product/security boundary call.
